approachQuestion.prompt:
Rearrange Review Tickets

A finite acyclic singly linked list stores integer priorities. Given threshold t, return the same nodes with all priorities below t first, followed by priorities at least t. Preserve original relative order within each group, each node identity and value. Change only next links. Only head and t are supplied; 0 <= n <= 200000; values and t are signed 32-bit integers.

Input: A(7) -> B(2) -> C(5) -> D(1), t=5. Output: B -> D -> A -> C -> null.
Input: [3,3], t=3. Output: the original order.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Walk once, saving each successor and detaching the current node. Append it to the tail of one of two chains according to its priority; join the below-threshold chain to the other at the end.
options.feedback: Tail appends preserve each group's encounter order, and detaching nodes prevents old links from leaking across groups.

options.text: Collect below-threshold references and remaining references in two arrays in encounter order, concatenate them and relink the nodes.
options.feedback: The arrays preserve the required order, but retain references that two head/tail pairs can replace.

options.text: Build each group by prepending encountered nodes to its head, then concatenate the groups.
options.feedback: For [7,2,5,1] this reverses each group, returning [1,2,5,7] instead of [2,1,7,5].

options.text: Sort all nodes by priority and relink them.
options.feedback: For A(7) -> B(5) with t=5, sorting puts B before A, violating within-group stability.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-08-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: Each node is classified and appended once; the final join is constant work. Inputs with arbitrary priorities require reading every node in the worst case. Two head/tail pairs and saved successors take constant space; original nodes constitute the output.
